column1: “Fuel is ₦1,400 a litre. How do you expect us to survive?”
column2: That's a real burden, and I won't pretend otherwise. The subsidy had become too expensive for the country, eating about 70% of federal revenue. About two-thirds of the money saved now goes to states and local governments, so your governor and council chairman should be showing you what they've done with it.
column3: Finance Ministry: ₦15.8tn saved June 2023–Dec 2025; FG ₦5.43tn, states ₦6.52tn, LGs ₦3.88tn.

column1: “The government pocketed all the subsidy money.”
column2: That's not what the figures show. By the Finance Ministry's estimate, about two-thirds of the savings went to states and local governments, not Abuja. Every tier should account for its share, and you have the right to ask your state.
column3: States received about ₦9.17tn and LGs ₦6.66tn above the pre-removal monthly rate (June 2023–Dec 2025).

column1: “There were no palliatives. We got nothing.”
column2: I understand many people didn't receive anything directly. There were programmes: cash transfers, a new minimum wage, CNG buses and student loans. But they didn't reach everyone. Cash transfers had reached 5.5 million of 15 million targeted households in 2024, so coverage still needs to grow.
column3: IMF 2025 Article IV report. Don't claim every Nigerian received a palliative.

column1: “Dangote's refinery should have made petrol cheap.”
column2: Many people expected that. Local refining makes supply more secure, but pump prices still follow world crude prices and the exchange rate. When crude rose in 2026, Nigerian prices rose too, even with the refinery running.
column3: Sept 2026: refinery at ~700,000 bpd; gantry price ₦1,350/litre (Reuters).

column1: “The removal was rushed and left us without a safety net.”
column2: That criticism has some truth: support took time to scale up. The government says the country couldn't afford a slow phase-out. What matters now is getting the support that exists to the people who need it.
column3: IMF (2024) said compensation was not scaled up in time. Acknowledge; don't argue.

column1: Name four claims callers must never make about the subsidy.
column2: 1) It alone caused all inflation. 2) Every Nigerian got a palliative. 3) The refinery guarantees cheap fuel. 4) Falling inflation means the cost of living has fallen.
